title: Ed’s note to the story cabinet volunteers
titleZh: 艾德給故事櫃志工的便條
passage:
We still need one recording for the courtyard gathering. Before picking it, check the two spaces on the story cabinet card. The speaker space tells us whom to credit; the listening space tells us whether to use a loudspeaker or keep the recording for the cabinet headphones. Neighbors can leave written comments even for a story marked “with headphones.” For the weekly comments sheet, print a neighbor’s response as a separate entry that gives the story title. Hosts may lightly edit a response, but a reader should still be able to tell which words the neighbor added and which came from the recording. A voice listed on the cabinet card is a speaker in the recording, not a byline for the comments sheet. The opening question for the courtyard audience is about a neighbor changing a plan, not about the weather. Give listeners enough context to know what the person was about to do, but leave them to notice what changed the plan.

I had suggested the opening minute of Mina’s long interview. The card says “with headphones,” and Mina’s aunt is only heard briefly near the end, so I thought the opening might be different. Gita reminded me that the aunt signed the speaker space but hasn’t agreed to a listening arrangement. With two voices, the listening entry is provisional until both speakers agree. Volunteers can rehearse with headphones in the meantime, but the restriction applies to the whole recording, not just the parts with both voices.

Gita pointed me to Mina’s other recording, “Rain on the Balcony,” which came in last month and has no other voice. Its current dated card says “play aloud.” Mina asked not to use her full name at this gathering. The older card has the full name, but the latest card gives the credit as Mina R. In that recording Mina says she took her washing basket out to the balcony as the first drops fell. She had planned to bring in her own clothes. Then she saw her new neighbor trying to pull in a long sheet without letting it touch the wet railing. She put the basket down and reached across to hold the near end. Afterward she wrote, ‘People keep asking where the rain drove me. It didn't drive me anywhere.’ It is all right to keep the full name in the cabinet’s index so volunteers can find her recordings.

If the speakers of an interview later agree to a different arrangement, date a replacement card and put the earlier one behind it. Please leave the original intact. When selecting a recording, use the dated card on top to check the current arrangement; the name printed on the recording doesn’t decide how we play it. One last note for the person on the microphone: please read the credit for this gathering as it appears on the latest card. The emcee only needs to say it once.
passageZh:
庭院聚會還需要一段錄音。挑選前，請查看故事櫃卡片上的兩個欄位：講述者欄寫應署名給誰；聆聽方式欄寫可以用揚聲器播放，還是只能在故事櫃用耳機聽。即使故事標註「用耳機聆聽」，鄰居仍可留下書面意見。 每週的意見單上，請把鄰居的回應獨立刊登，並註明故事標題。主持人可略作編修，但讀者仍要看得出哪些是鄰居補充的話、哪些來自錄音。故事櫃卡片上列的是錄音的講述者，不是意見單的作者署名。 庭院聚會開場會請大家想想，一位鄰居為什麼改變原來的打算，而不是討論天氣。請先讓聽眾知道她原本要做什麼，但把改變計畫的原因留給聽眾自己發現。

我原先提議播米娜長訪談開頭的一分鐘。卡片寫著「用耳機聆聽」，米娜的阿姨只在錄音快結束時短暫出聲，所以我以為開頭也許能另作處理。吉塔提醒我，阿姨在講述者欄簽了名，但還沒同意聆聽方式。有兩位講述者時，聆聽方式在雙方同意前都只是暫定。這段期間志工可以用耳機排練，但限制適用於整段錄音，不只兩人都出聲的片段。

吉塔請我看看米娜上個月送來的另一段錄音〈陽台上的雨〉，裡頭只有她的聲音。這段錄音目前採用的日期卡寫著「可公開播放」。米娜希望這次聚會不要使用她的全名。舊卡上有全名，但最新版卡片署名為 Mina R.。 錄音裡米娜說，才剛開始下雨，她就拿著洗衣籃走到陽台，原本要把自己的衣服收進屋。接著她看到剛搬來的鄰居正努力把長床單拉進屋，不想讓床單碰到濕欄杆。她把籃子放下，伸手過去扶住靠近她的那一端。後來她寫道：「大家一直問我下雨把我趕到哪裡去了。雨沒有把我趕到哪裡去。」 只要留在故事櫃的索引裡，完整姓名可以保留，方便志工查找她的錄音。

如果訪談的講述者後來都同意改用另一種聆聽方式，請在新卡上註明日期，將舊卡放在新卡後面。不要改動原卡。選擇錄音時，請依最上面那張有日期的卡確認現行方式；錄音上印的人名不決定播放方式。 再提醒一下拿麥克風的人：請照最新版卡片上的署名，在這次聚會唸出講述者的名字。司儀只需唸一次。
